title: Identity-resolution horizontal map factors through the vertical sections comparison
statement: Let $Z$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $G,F$ be $\mathcal O_Z$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\psi:G\to F$ a morphism. Fix any resolution data $D$ for the identity-scheme map [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]: injective resolutions $I$ of $F$ and $J$ of $G$, a natural-indexed injective complex $K$, a quasi-isomorphism $\lambda:(\mathrm{id}_Z)_*I\to K$, a map $\beta:J\to K$ satisfying the augmentation equation, and the pinned sections isomorphism $a:\Gamma(Z,I)\to\Gamma(Z,(\mathrm{id}_Z)_*I)$. Let $\alpha:J\to I$ be the standard descent of $\psi$ between the two injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every $p\in\mathbb N$, on the homology of the underlying additive sections complexes one has $H^p(\Gamma\beta)=H^p(\mu)\circ H^p(\Gamma\alpha)$, where $\mu=(\Gamma\lambda)\circ a$. This asserts only an identity of maps between sections-complex homologies; no transport to right derived functors is included.

source.place: Remark 01FB, identity-scheme specialization; homotopy uniqueness from Derived Categories Tag 013S.

proof.text: Take the standard resolution descent alpha of psi. Use the inverse identity-pushforward comparison degreewise to define l : I to K by composing it with lambda. The augmentation formula for alpha and the compatibility equation for beta imply equality of their composites with the augmentation of J.

Extend J and K by zero to integer indices. K is bounded below termwise injective and the augmentation of J is a quasi-isomorphism. Uniqueness up to homotopy after that quasi-isomorphism gives beta homotopic to alpha followed by l. Restrict the homotopy back to natural indices. The additive sections functor preserves the homotopy, so taking homology gives H(Gamma beta) = H(Gamma l) composed with H(Gamma alpha).

The component formula pinning a to restriction along the equality id^{-1}(Z)=Z identifies a with Gamma of the inverse pushforward-identity comparison. Substitute Gamma l = a followed by Gamma lambda into the preceding homology equation.
